To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
women who were successful in achieving their family-planning goals had a lower embedded-figures score than women who failed in achieving their goals.
women with a high degree of field independence and a low degree of field dependence were more successful in implementing family-planning behavior than women with a low degree of independence.
women who scored high on embedded-figures tests were more successful at achieving their family-planning goals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a number of factors which influence success in achieving a family-planning goal.
the relationship between locus of control of reinforcers, a personality variable, and the ability to implement family-planning goals, a behavior variable.
the relationship between the ability to implement goals and the ability to perceive relationships among elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the embedded-figures test is a valid measure of success at implementation of family-planning goals.
the internal-external locus-of-control dimension is not related to success at implementation of family-planning goals.
internal-external locus and embedded-figures measures are not related to success at goal implementation, but that embedded-figures scores are related to success at implementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women high on embedded figures, low on internal-external locus, or high on embedded-figures, low on internal locus, were more successful at implementing family planning goals than were other women.
the more successful women were more field-independent and less internal than the less successful women.
the internal-external locus measure does not predict family-planning success, while the embedded-figures measure does.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the EFT is a valid and useful tool in assessing field dependence/independence.
the field-dependence-independence construct is an important predictor of success in implementing family-planning behavior.
the use of the embedded-figures test to assess field dependence— independence is not recommended.
